answer: Per-Capability Pigment Ledger: each capability class (e.g., transact, publish) carries a scarce, non-transferable pigment minted only through sustained useful work in that class. A new identity starts with a fixed onyx budget of zero-EV capability slots, so clones must first earn pigment at a cost exceeding expected gain. Enforcement caps concurrent capability use per pigment unit, and cloning splits pigment, raising marginal cost. Each extra identity also pays a recurring pearl audit fee for independent liveness checks, making the marginal clone strictly negative-EV.
